\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Unique Games: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Recovery of encoded natural number rows]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseNatRows_encodeNatRows}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseNatRows_encodeNatRows}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.encodeNatRows, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseNatRows}
For every finite list of finite lists of natural numbers, parsing its natural number row
encoding returns exactly the original list of rows.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recovery of encoded unique games]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseUniqueGame_encodeUniqueGame}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseUniqueGame_encodeUniqueGame}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.UniqueGameConstraint, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.UniqueGameConstraint.Valid, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.encodeUniqueGame, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseUniqueGame}
Let $q$ be a natural number and let $G$ be a finite list of unique game constraints.
Suppose each constraint has distinct left and right variable indices, and its table is a
permutation of $0,1,\ldots,q-1$. Parsing the unique game encoding of $G$ with parameter
$q$ returns exactly $G$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recovery of encoded max cut edges]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseMaxCut_encodeMaxCut}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseMaxCut_encodeMaxCut}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.encodeMaxCut, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseMaxCut}
Let $E$ be a finite list of ordered pairs of natural numbers, and suppose the two
entries of every pair in $E$ are distinct. Parsing the max cut encoding of $E$ returns
exactly $E$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Validity of the encoded Max-Cut graph]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph_valid}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph_valid}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.IsValid, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph}
Let $E$ be a nonempty finite list of ordered pairs of natural numbers, none of which is
a loop. The weighted directed graph formed from $E$ has nonnegative symmetric weights,
total ordered-pair weight $1$, and zero diagonal weights.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cut value of the encoded graph]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph_cutValue}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph_cutValue}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutVertexBound}
Let $E$ be any finite list of ordered pairs of natural numbers, let $F$ label the
vertices indexed below the variable bound of $E$ by Boolean values, and let $f:\mathbb
N\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose $F(v)=f(v)$ at every such vertex. In the weighted directed graph
formed from $E$, the cut value of $F$ equals the number of entries $(u,v)$ of $E$ with
$f(u)\ne f(v)$, divided by the length of $E$; repeated entries are counted with
multiplicity, and when $E$ is empty both sides are interpreted by the displayed real
quotient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Separating a promise pair preserves NP-hardness]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.PromiseNPHard.separating_language}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.PromiseNPHard.separating_language}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.PromiseNPHard, Complexity.NPHard}
Let $Y,N,L$ be languages of binary strings. Suppose $Y$ and $N$ are disjoint, and every
language in NP has a polynomial-time map sending its members into $Y$ and its nonmembers
into $N$. If $Y\subseteq L$ and $N\cap L=\varnothing$, then $L$ is NP-hard under
polynomial-time many-one reductions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Unique Games hardness of Max-Cut]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCut_ug_hard}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCut_ug_hard}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.PromiseNPHard, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.UniqueGamesConjecture, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutNo, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutYes}
Let $\pi/2<\theta<\pi$ and $\delta>0$, and suppose $\theta/\pi+\delta<(1-\cos\theta)/2$.
If the Unique Games Conjecture holds, then the promise problem whose yes-instances
encode nonempty edge lists with Max-Cut optimum at least $(1-\cos\theta)/2$ and whose
no-instances encode nonempty edge lists with optimum less than $\theta/\pi+\delta$ is
Promise-NP-hard.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[NP-hardness from Max-Cut promise separation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCut_ug_hard_separating_language}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCut_ug_hard_separating_language}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.UniqueGamesConjecture, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutNo, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutYes, Complexity.NPHard}
Let $\pi/2<\theta<\pi$, assume the Unique Games Conjecture, and let $L$ be a language of
binary strings. If $L$ contains every encoded nonempty edge list whose associated
Max-Cut optimum is at least $(1-\cos\theta)/2$, and is disjoint from the encoded
nonempty edge lists whose optimum is less than $\theta/\pi$, then $L$ is NP-hard under
polynomial-time many-one reductions.
\end{theorem}
